samples.question: Exactly two blocks in this picture are drawn with a solid black border; every other block or mark is drawn in colour and is decoration. The black-bordered square block is the panel: it is divided into a 5 by 5 grid of 25 equal square cells, and each cell is filled with one flat gray taken from a set of exactly four different grays. The other black-bordered block is the key: it shows two flat gray swatches side by side or one above the other, and each swatch gray is one of the four grays used in the panel. Carry out this operation: mark every panel cell whose gray matches either of the two swatch grays in the key, and leave every other panel cell unmarked. The order of the two swatches does not matter. The marked cells form exactly one symbol on the 5 by 5 grid: 'ring' is the eight cells of the 3 by 3 centre block without its middle cell, 'cross' is the four corner cells together with the four cells diagonally inside them, 'arrow' is a centre column of three cells rising into a three-cell bar with one cell above its middle and one cell out at each side below it, and 'stair' is an eight-cell staircase of horizontal pairs stepping down from the top-left corner to the bottom right. Every symbol marks exactly 8 of the 25 cells. The panel shows two of these symbols superposed and does not by itself say which one is marked; only the key's two grays decide that. Which symbol do the marked cells form? Answer with exactly one of: arrow, cross, ring, stair.
